Title: #NSTviral: Motorcyclist's roadside rescue with cat sparks debate
Article:
Ahmad Mukhsein Mukhtar
KUALA LUMPUR: An unusual roadside rescue involving a motorcyclist, a cat and a stranded food delivery rider has captured the attention of Malaysians online.
The 22-second clip, posted on TikTok by user @_mses, shows the motorcyclist travelling along a highway in the capital with a cat clinging to him.
At the same time, the rider uses his foot to push a stranded food delivery rider's motorcycle from behind, helping him continue his journey.
"The type of things you see on the road," the user captioned the video, which has garnered more than 485,000 views and 68,000 likes.
Some viewers found the unusual rescue amusing and were impressed by how calmly the cat remained on the moving motorcycle.
"The cat is so cute," user @m1noo wrote.
User @shazwaniemyzl joked that the cat would probably return home and tell its friends that it had helped tow a motorcycle.
Meanwhile, @hazeem.syhr wondered how anyone could find a cat brave enough to ride on a motorcycle without becoming frightened.
Others, however, expressed concern that carrying the cat in such a manner on a highway could endanger both the animal and other road users.
User @sangkepalabesi said he occasionally took his cat on motorcycle rides but warned that bringing one onto a highway was dangerous.
"Do not endanger the cat and other road users just because you want fame," he wrote.
User @amjsigma, who identified as a cat lover, also said the situation was no laughing matter.
"I do not like seeing people carry cats like this on a highway," the user wrote.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nga: Chennah, Repah losses a bitter lesson for DAP
Article:
SEREMBAN: DAP accepts the outcome of the Negri Sembilan state election with an open heart and respects the mandate delivered by voters, says party deputy chairman Datuk Seri Nga Kor Ming.
Although the result fell short of Pakatan Harapan's (PH) expectations, Nga said the coalition accepted the outcome and would conduct a thorough post-mortem to address its shortcomings.
"The defeats in the Chennah and Repah state constituencies are a difficult and bitter experience for us. However, PH will not lose heart.
"Instead, we will reflect, carry out a comprehensive assessment and work towards regaining victory in Negri Sembilan in the future," he said in a statement today.
Nga, who is also Housing and Local Government Minister, said DAP would remain steadfast in its struggle, face challenges together, and move forward with determination.
He added that DAP and PH would continue serving the people with full commitment to regain public confidence through their performance and service record.
In the election, DAP won nine of the 11 state seats it contested.
In Chennah, party secretary-general Anthony Loke lost to MCA candidate Siow Kong Choon by a majority of 688 votes, while PH narrowly lost Repah to a Barisan Nasional candidate by 444 votes.
Nga expressed appreciation to Loke for leading the campaign with dedication and thanked Negri Sembilan voters for their support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Don't pressure Aminuddin to vacate MB's official residence
Article:
SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun should not be pressured to vacate the official Menteri Besar's residence, recalling that similar pressure was placed on Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan in 2023.
Instead, Zahid said there should be humanity among political leaders.
"It should not happen like that. In my opinion, give time, even though the new menteri besar may be sworn in as soon as possible.
"They are all our friends. We must have a sense of humanity and ethics that we should use to respect our friends," he said.
He said this when met by reporters outside Istana Hinggap Negri Sembilan here last night.

Title: Saleswoman loses RM290,000 to investment scam, fake recovery agent
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A 61-year-old supermarket saleswoman lost RM290,910 after falling victim to an online investment scheme and a scammer posing as an officer promising to recover her money.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim lodged a report at 12.59pm yesterday after realising she had been duped by an investment scheme advertised on Facebook since May.
He said the victim was attracted by low-capital offers promising high returns in a short period, leading her to make initial capital payments and several additional transactions to redeem her alleged profits.
"After all payments were made, the victim did not receive the promised returns. She was then contacted by an person claiming to be an officer handling online fraud cases, who offered to help recover her lost money, but she was again asked to make payments," he said.
Azli said the victim, believing the claims, made 57 transactions to 16 different bank accounts between June 14 and July 31.
The total losses amounted to RM290,910, involving her personal savings and proceeds from pawning gold.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.

Title: Brazilian man stabs three to death at factory, later found dead
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: A Brazilian man who fatally stabbed three people at a factory in Sao Paulo was later found dead after his arrest.
The 33-year-old man entered his workplace on Saturday before stabbing three people, aged 39 to 54, AFP reported.
He was then arrested and taken to a police station, where he was later found dead. Police have ruled it a suicide.
According to local media, the man, a forklift operator, had gone to the factory on his day off to kill two people.
The third victim is believed to have been killed while trying to stop the attack.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: N9 polls: Siti Nur Umaira youngest winner, Mohamad Hasan oldest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thirty-five-year-old Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Siti Nur Umaira Hasim emerged as the youngest winner of the 16th Negri Sembilan election yesterday, while UMNO deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan was the oldest at 70.
Siti Nur Umaira, the Rasah UMNO Puteri division chief, secured 14,209 votes to win the seat with a majority of 5,279 votes, defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Ahmad Faez Abdul Razak (8,930 votes) and Bersatu incumbent Mohamad Hanifah Abu Baker (1,985 votes).
The result saw BN wrest the Labu state seat from Mohamad Hanifah, who won it under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) ticket in the 2023 state polls.
Labu, which has 32,884 registered voters, is one of five state seats under the Rasah parliamentary constituency.
Meanwhile, Mohamad retained the Rantau state seat by securing 19,050 votes to defeat PH's Dr Azizul Hakim Mahdi (7,032 votes) in a straight fight.
The Foreign Minister defended the seat with a majority of 12,018 votes, up from the 10,280 votes he polled in the 2023 state election.
Meanwhile, PN's Kamarol Ridzuan Mohd Zain retained the Paroi state seat with the largest majority of the election, securing a 16,959-vote majority.
He polled 32,004 votes in a three-cornered fight, defeating PH's Ahmad Shahir Mohd Shah (15,045 votes) and Bersatu's Mohd Nazree Mohd Yunus (2,205 votes).
Kamarol Ridzuan's winning majority also more than tripled the 5,539 votes he secured in the 2023 state polls.
The 16th Negri Sembilan election saw 103 candidates vying for 36 state seats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Capital One says it closed Trump Organisation's accounts after anti-money laundering probe
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: Capital One Financial hit back on Friday against a lawsuit over its decision to close the Trump Organisation's bank accounts years ago, stating that it did so after a review by anti-money laundering experts.
The disclosure marks the first time a bank has formally linked money laundering concerns to US President Donald Trump's family business. Capital One is seeking to dismiss the case by casting doubt on claims of illegally debanking — or denying services on religious or political grounds — the Trump Organisation.
The Trump Organisation and Capital One did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Capital One has never accused the Trump Organisation of illegal money laundering. But Friday's filing argues that "documents and Plaintiffs' own allegations make clear that Capital One closed Plaintiffs' accounts for anti-money laundering (AML) reasons.
The closures were the result of months of analysis and a careful review by Capital One's AML team in accordance with bank policies and regulatory guidance."
Capital One gave notice of its plans to close more than 300 Trump-affiliated bank accounts in March 2021. The Trump Organisation and Eric Trump, the president's son, filed a lawsuit in March 2025 in a Florida federal court, alleging the accounts were closed because of Capital One's "woke" beliefs and its desire to benefit from the political mood after the January 6, 2021 riot at the US Capitol.
'MISGUIDED' ALLEGATIONS: CAPITAL ONE
The federal court in Miami has tossed two complaints in the Capital One case, but gave the plaintiffs opportunities each time to submit an amended complaint. Capital One said that the latest version, filed in July, "suffers from the same fundamental flaws as their prior two pleadings".
Capital One said in Friday's filing that the Trump Organization's allegations of political pretext were "misguided" and "based on cherry-picked quotations unsupported by the full context" of documents submitted to the court.
"The transaction patterns identified by Capital One are among the types of activity flagged by federal banking guidance," the filing said.
Since the start of Trump's second term, his administration has put pressure on some large banks, echoing conservative complaints that the institutions are deliberately targeting the political right. Trump signed an executive order in August 2025 barring discriminatory debanking.
In January, Trump filed a suit against JPMorgan Chase on the same grounds, underscoring the fraught policy environment Wall Street is navigating during the president's second term.
In 2019, during his first term, Trump sued Capital One and Deutsche Bank in an attempt to prevent them from sharing financial records with Congress as part of a probe led by Democratic lawmakers. Anti-money laundering professionals at Deutsche Bank reportedly flagged a set of transactions, but executives ignored them; Deutsche Bank denied the report at the time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israeli strikes kill at least four in Gaza despite Trump announcing breakthrough
Article:
CAIRO: Israeli airstrikes continued in Gaza for a second straight day on Sunday, killing at least four Palestinians, despite US President Donald Trump's announcement of a breakthrough in efforts to implement last year's Gaza ceasefire agreement.
Palestinian health officials said Israeli warplanes carried out separate strikes in Gaza City and Deir al-Balah.
A man and his wife were killed and four people were wounded in an airstrike on an apartment in Deir al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip, while two more people, including a child, were killed in a strike on an apartment in Gaza City, medics said.
Trump said on Thursday there had been a breakthrough after Hamas agreed to disarm under a US-backed initiative to implement the ceasefire agreement reached last year in Egypt. On Friday, Trump's Board of Peace published a 15-point roadmap setting out the final steps for implementing the agreement.
The roadmap has yet to be implemented. Hamas has said it will hand over its weapons for storage only after Israel halts military operations and withdraws its forces in line with last year's agreement.
An Israeli official told Reuters there would be no withdrawal from the military's current positions unless Hamas undergoes "genuine disarmament".
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has not commented publicly on the initiative, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has called it unacceptable and said Israel should continue assassinating Hamas leaders.
Former senior Fatah official Mohammed Dahlan, who is based in the United Arab Emirates, said in a Facebook post that Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law and a senior adviser involved in the US initiative, had told him he was working with the Israeli side to stop attacks on Gaza.
Dahlan said contacts with the US were continuing to ensure the agreement was fully implemented, adding that its success now depended on Israel fully ending its daily attacks on Gaza.
Reuters has reached out to the US State Department for comment on Dahlan's remarks. There was no immediate comment from Israel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor to review stray animal management SOPs across all local authorities
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor state government will review the standard operating procedures (SOPs) for managing stray animals across all local authorities to ensure enforcement operations are carried out more effectively, safely and humanely.
Local Government and Tourism Committee chairman Datuk Ng Suee Lim said the review would include training programmes, operational procedures and closer collaboration with the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and other stakeholders.
"The state government remains committed to safeguarding public safety, while at the same time enhancing animal welfare practices and upholding public trust in the integrity and professionalism of government agencies," he said in a statement yesterday.
Ng said the state government also expressed its appreciation for the advice of Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, who emphasised the importance of compassion towards animals and the principle that no one is above the law.
"Such values will continue to guide the state government's policies and decisions," he said.
Ng said his office was also aware of the police report filed by the Klang Royal City Council (MBDK) following the death of a dog during a stray dog enforcement operation carried out in Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang.
He said the state government would leave it entirely to the police to conduct an independent, transparent and professional investigation, while urging all parties to respect the process and refrain from speculation.
"The Selangor state government regrets the incident and considers it a serious matter, as public safety and animal welfare are responsibilities that must be carefully balanced.
"Every enforcement operation must be carried out professionally, responsibly and in compliance with the law and established standard operating procedures," he said.
Earlier, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin expressed sadness, disappointment and anger over ongoing cases of cruelty towards pets and stray animals, particularly dogs and cats, which have recently gained attention online.
Istana Alam Shah said Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin also urged the federal government to reassess the penalties under the Animal Welfare Act 2015 to ensure stricter punishment for animal cruelty offenders and more consistent enforcement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Expert urges KLIA security, aviation safety review after Malaysia Airlines pilot's drug arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia over a drug smuggling attempt has exposed weaknesses in both aviation safety oversight and airport security systems at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), an aviation expert said.
Associate Professor Dr Mohd Harridon Mohamed Suffian said the incident should prompt a comprehensive review of drug detection programmes and security screening procedures for airline staff at KLIA.
"This case highlights the possibility that drug abuse among airline employees, including flight crew and technical personnel, may not have been detected through existing monitoring mechanisms.
"The issue should serve as a catalyst for authorities in Malaysia and abroad to review the effectiveness of the Drug Detection Programme implemented by Malaysia Airlines," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Harridon, from the Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School, said this was fundamentally a safety issue, particularly in light of allegations that the pilot, who was the second officer, was intoxicated while operating the aircraft.
"Such allegations, if proven, have serious implications because safety is always the highest priority in aviation."
Harridon said Malaysia Airlines should conduct an in-depth internal inquiry into how the alleged breakdown occurred and strengthen periodic drug testing for all technical crew, cabin crew, engineers and other  staff.
Malaysia Airlines on Friday said it was conducting an internal review.
Harridon said more frequent and stringent screening could help detect substance abuse before it affected flight operations.
He said investigators must also determine how the suspected drugs allegedly passed through airport security undetected.
"It is imperative to identify whether there were weaknesses within the security system at KLIA.
"Such incidents can undermine public confidence in the airport's security standards and negatively affect Malaysia's reputation as an international aviation hub."
Harridon said the incident required a coordinated response involving Malaysia Airlines, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia and other relevant agencies to review existing protocols, regulations and enforcement procedures.
He also proposed introducing stronger peer-reporting mechanisms within airlines to detect behavioural changes  that could indicate substance abuse.
"There must be a system that enables colleagues to report signs of impairment so immediate intervention can take place before safety is compromised," he said.
Harridon also recommended periodic mental health screening, saying such assessments could identify individuals requiring early intervention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CAAM probes security procedures after Malaysia Airlines pilot's drug arrest [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) is investigating whether all aviation security procedures were followed after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested in Jakarta over alleged drug smuggling.
CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the incident, which is under investigation by Indonesian authorities, would also be assessed from a regulatory perspective, including the airline's compliance with aviation security requirements and the airport operator's screening processes before the pilot departed Malaysia.
"Like all other persons entering the Security Restricted Area, aircrew are required to undergo security screening before being granted access. There are no blanket exemptions from these screening requirements," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Norazman said all passengers and aircrew, together with their carry-on baggage and personal belongings, were subject to the same security screening before entering restricted airport areas using approved screening methods and equipment, including X-ray screening of baggage.
[[nid:1502437]]
"The screening process is conducted by airport operators and security personnel in accordance with the Civil Aviation Security Regulations 2019 and the National Civil Aviation Security Programme  before crew members are allowed access to the airside or other restricted areas."
Responding to questions on how such a large quantity of drugs could have gone undetected, CAAM said the matter remained under investigation and that it was gathering all relevant facts."
Earlier last  week, Indonesian authorities announced the arrest of a 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after allegedly discovering 25kg of ecstasy and methamphetamine concealed in his luggage.
The drugs, comprising more than 70,000 capsules, were estimated to be worth RM45 million in the Indonesian market.
A urine test on the 39-year-old pilot also revealed traces of methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine.
It was also reported that the pilot told investigators this was the third time he had attempted to smuggle drugs — the second to Indonesia and once in Malaysia.
He also allegedly told investigators that he had been promised some RM50,000 to deliver the narcotics in this latest case.
Norazman said CAAM would determine whether all applicable regulatory requirements and security procedures had been complied with before his departure from Malaysia.
"CAAM is working to establish the facts and will take any necessary regulatory action within its jurisdiction should any non-compliance with aviation regulations be identified."
On reports that the pilot had allegedly tested positive for drugs, he said Malaysia already has a  regulatory framework governing alcohol and drug management for aviation personnel.
He said under the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016, flight crew were prohibited from performing duties while under the influence of alcohol, drugs or any psychoactive substance.
He added that every Malaysian Air Operator Certificate  holder is also required to implement a CAAM-approved Alcohol and Drug Management Programme  under Civil Aviation Directive  6007.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran threatens to strike other nations' energy fields if US launches fresh attacks
Article:
CAIRO: Iran warned this weekend against any "adventurous action" by the US and said it would retaliate decisively if American forces follow through on President Donald Trump's threats of fresh attacks on Iranian targets.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi's comments in separate phone calls on Saturday with senior Turkish, Pakistani and Saudi officials came just hours after Kuwait's army said it destroyed hostile drones launched by Iran against several vital facilities.
Speaking to Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Araqchi said Iran would respond decisively to any "aggression" and discussed the consequences of "destabilising actions" by the US, as well as prospects for heightened regional insecurity, according to Araqchi's Telegram account.
Araqchi later told Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan that any attacks by the US and Israel or participation by regional countries in such actions would be met with a "proportionate response."
Nournews, a media outlet affiliated with Iran's top security body, said on Saturday that US attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure would prompt Iranian strikes on oil fields in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, as well as the gas fields of Qatar and Israel, saying "all will be burned to ashes."
At a cabinet meeting on Friday at the Camp David retreat, Trump said he believed US negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, could still reach a deal with Iran.
But Trump also said he was losing faith in the Iranians, saying "they break their word so often" — a claim that Teheran has frequently levelled at Washington — and said he would be "hitting them."
[[nid:1502425]]
STRAIT OF HORMUZ
Oil prices have stayed high since US and Israeli forces started the war with strikes on Iran on February 28. Trump has argued that his stated goal of keeping Iran from gaining nuclear weapons justifies higher fuel costs in the near term, but the economic pain has put political pressure on him to find a way to end the war. Benchmark Brent crude futures rose 24 per cent in July, and analysts polled by Reuters expect prices to rise further this year.
The risk of Iranian attacks has deterred most shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, an important conduit for global energy supplies, since the start of the conflict, sending shockwaves through the world economy.
A government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian property belonging to a company on Bubiyan Island were hit on Saturday, with falling shrapnel causing material damage but no casualties, the Kuwaiti army said.
Adding to the energy industry's concerns, Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen recently began threatening the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait at the other end of the Red Sea from the Suez Canal, another export route for Saudi crude.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Saturday it had received reports of two maritime incidents off Oman, including one in which a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile that damaged the engine room. In the other incident, the master of a tanker reported seeing a large splash and an explosion close to the vessel, though no damage was reported.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 13 dead after small tourist plane crashes in Peru
Article:
LIMA: A small plane carrying foreign tourists to view Peru's famed Nazca Lines archaeological site crashed on Saturday, killing all 13 people on board, police said.
The incident occurred shortly after 1pm (1800 GMT) after the plane took off from the airport in Pisco, located about 240 kilometres (150 miles) south of the capital, Lima.
"We have information that 11 passengers and two crew members have died," Police Major Jorge Andrade told reporters at the crash site.
"Given the severity of the accident, there are no survivors. We have recovered four bodies so far," Andrade said, without identifying the victims.
He also did not give any immediate indication of what may have caused the crash. Peru's civil aviation authority will investigate, and agents were already at the scene collecting evidence.
Firefighters and police were working amid the twisted, smouldering wreckage of the aircraft, according to images posted on Facebook by local news outlets.
The foreign trade ministry issued a statement saying the 11 passengers were "foreign tourists", adding that it would offer assistance to the embassies involved.
RPP radio reported that seven Italians, two Germans and two Spaniards were killed.
IN-FLIGHT EMERGENCY
The Nazca Lines are a group of geoglyphs etched into the desert sands that date back to between 500 BC and 500 AD.
The meaning of the geometric shapes and animal outlines remains a mystery, with some believing they had ritual astronomical functions, according to UNESCO, which declared the area a World Heritage Site in 1994.
The doomed plane was operated by AeroDiana, which offers sightseeing trips lasting 30 minutes to an hour over the site, which is best seen from the air.
AeroDiana told AFP that it would soon release more information about the crash.
Municipal officials in Vista Alegre, where the plane crashed, said in a statement that preliminary information indicated an "in-flight emergency" was to blame, without offering more details.
One resident of Vista Alegre said the plane exploded on impact.
Dozens of small planes operate from the airport in Pisco, handling a large volume of mostly foreign tourists hoping to visit the Nazca Lines.
Such accidents have occurred before. In 2022, seven people were killed in a plane crash, including two Chileans and three Dutch nationals.
In October 2010, four British tourists and two Peruvian crew members died when an AirNasca plane crashed after taking the tourists to view the site.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja, team killed in Pakistan avalanche
Article:
SKARDU: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja and his nine climbing companions were killed in an avalanche in Pakistan during an ascent of one of the world's highest mountains, his expedition company said on Saturday, as rescuers tackled treacherous conditions to recover their bodies.
The avalanche struck on Thursday, cutting off contact with the international expedition led by Purja, a 43-year-old British-Nepali climber, on Broad Peak in northern Pakistan.
"It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak," Purja's company, Elite Expeditions, said on social media.
"We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive," it said.
The remains recovered so far – flown by helicopter to hospital for formal identification – included an American woman, an Omani woman and a Nepali man, the regional government said in a statement released on Friday night.
Purja, who served with Britain's Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Service of the Royal Marines, broke multiple climbing records after becoming a full-time mountaineer and expedition guide.
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah offered his condolences over the deaths of Purja and the other climbers, which he said "has shocked us."
"The physical journey of all the deceased climbers... has been interrupted, but the history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring," Shah said in a statement on social media.
Rana Sanaullah, the Pakistani prime minister's adviser for provincial coordination, said four bodies had been recovered so far and the search was continuing on Saturday by air, ground and GPS tracking despite adverse weather.
"The Broad Peak tragedy is deeply heartbreaking. Pakistan stands in solidarity with the people of Nepal in this time of grief," he said in a statement.
Rescuers and military helicopters scoured the area while teams stayed at the base camp overnight, according to the Gilgit-Baltistan regional government.
"The rescue operation is being conducted under extremely challenging terrain and high-altitude weather conditions by the Pakistani army in coordination with local high-altitude climbers and rescuers," it said.
The disaster prompted an outpouring of grief in Nepal and across the wider mountaineering community.
Italian climbing great Reinhold Messner, who made the first solo ascent of Everest, paid tribute to Purja, saying his thoughts were with his friends and family.
"Nirmal chose his own path with courage and passion. What remains is not only the sorrow of his passing but the memory of a life truly lived," he said in a post on Instagram.
POWERFUL AVALANCHE
The avalanche struck while the mountaineers were attempting to summit Broad Peak (8,047 metres, or 26,400 feet) on Thursday at an altitude of around 6,600 metres, according to regional authorities.
[[nid:1502419]]
The expedition comprised 10 people – Purja, five Nepalis, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American and a climber from China.
The team was last in contact on Thursday morning, the official statement said, with reports emerging that evening of the powerful avalanche.
"Data from their tracking devices indicates that they were thrown hundreds of metres down the mountainside," Naila Kiani, of Pakistan's Alpine Club, told *Le Monde* newspaper.
Fida Ali, a climber in the area who had worked closely with Purja since 2023, told AFP the team's focus this climbing season was summiting Broad Peak, but they had first tackled G2 in harsh weather.
Ali also joined the expedition to Broad Peak in its initial stages but returned early to accompany a Russian climber who was suffering from exhaustion, narrowly avoiding the fatal avalanche.
"I wanted to go with him (Purja) but couldn't and came back with her. I was part of the team but survived," he told AFP.
SUPER PEAKS
Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, said Purja's death was a huge loss.
"He showed Nepalis that climbing doesn't have to be just work, that you can climb for your own fun and passion," he told AFP.
Purja had written on X this week that he was close to becoming the first person to climb all 14 "super peaks" twice without supplementary oxygen.
"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down," he wrote.
He climbed all 14 "eight-thousanders" (peaks above 8,000 metres) in six months and six days between April and October 2019, then a world record.
Broad Peak is the world's 12th-highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range in northern Pakistan, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technically challenging of all the 8,000-metre-plus climbs.
It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid submits three names to Negri Sembilan palace for MB post
Article:
SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has submitted three names to the Negri Sembilan palace for consideration as the state's next Menteri Besar.
Zahid said the final decision rests entirely with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, who has the prerogative to appoint one of the candidates.
"I have submitted three names to His Royal Highness and leave them to His Royal Highness's wisdom.
"It is His Royal Highness's absolute prerogative to choose one of the names as the next Menteri Besar of Negri Sembilan," he said after an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap here.
Zahid said all three candidates submitted were from BN.
He added that the palace would issue an official statement on the matter as soon as possible.
The Umno president said he had been granted an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
This comes after BN and Perikatan Nasional secured 25 seats to form the next state government in the Negri Sembilan state election.
Zahid said BN won 18 seats while PN secured seven, giving the coalition a total of 25 seats in the 36-member state assembly.
"With these 25 seats, subject to His Royal Highness's consent, a Barisan Nasional-led government will be formed in Negri Sembilan," he said.
When asked whether caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun would have to vacate his official residence immediately, Zahid said there was no need for that.
"They should be given some time. Although we may have political differences and compete against each other, they are all our friends.
"We must have a sense of humanity and observe proper etiquette in respecting one another," he said.

Title: EC confirms BN victory with 18 seats in Negri Sembilan
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Election Commission (EC) has officially announced that BN won 18 seats in the 16th Negri Sembilan election.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said PH secured 12 seats, while PN won seven.
He said Bersatu, Barisan Jemaah Islamiah Se-Malaysia (Berjasa), Parti Orang Asli Malaysia (Asli), Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) and four Independent candidates failed to win any seats.
"A total of 646,084 voters, or 72.64 per cent, cast their ballots. This includes early voters, postal voters and ordinary voters.
"Overall, the EC is satisfied with the polling process, which took place on Saturday, and registered voters were able to fulfil their rights and responsibilities," he said.
He said this at a press conference announcing the official results of the 16th Negri Sembilan election at Wisma Persekutuan here shortly after midnight.
Ramlan said the election was conducted smoothly without any untoward incidents that could have affected the electoral process.
"In carrying out election matters, the EC always complies with the relevant laws and regulations.
"Further details on the results of the 16th Negri Sembilan election can be obtained through the MySPR Semak application or the website at dashboard.spr.gov.my," he said.
A total of 103 candidates contested the 36 state seats in the election.
Of the total, PH fielded 36 candidates, followed by BN (25), Bersatu (24) and PN (11).
Berjasa, Asli and PSM each fielded one candidate, while four Independent candidates also contested.
A total of 21 constituencies saw three-cornered contests, 11 featured straight fights, while two constituencies each witnessed four-cornered and five-cornered contests.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chow: No need for Loke to step down immediately
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: There is no immediate need for Anthony Loke to step down as Negri Sembilan DAP chairman following the party's defeat in the state election, says Chow Kon Yeow.
Chow, a DAP central executive committee member, said Loke should be given time to regroup and rally party members before making any decision on his position, according to FMT.
"There is no need to consider (resigning) immediately.
"Let things settle down for a few days before making any decision," he told reporters after the opening of the George Town Festival.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, had said he would consider stepping down as the party's Negri Sembilan chairman after losing the Chennah seat in the Aug 1 state election.
Chow said Chennah had always been a difficult seat to defend because of its mixed demographic composition, and that BN's electoral pact with PN had compounded the challenge as PN supporters swung behind the BN candidate.
He added that the campaign had also taken on racial and religious overtones, making the contest even tougher for Loke.
According to unofficial results, Loke lost Chennah to MCA
candidate
Siow Kong Choon.
Loke had represented Chennah since 2013, successfully
defending
the seat in three consecutive state elections, most recently with a majority of 2,200 votes in 2023.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wan Saiful calls on Bersatu members to abandon 'sinking ship' after Negri results
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wawasan vice-president Datuk Wan Saiful Wan Jan has called on Bersatu members to abandon the party and join Wawasan.
Wan Saiful said the Negri Sembilan election results had made clear that Bersatu was no longer politically relevant.
"Do not let your struggle sink with the ship. The time has come for you to make a brave decision - come and move together with Parti Wawasan Negara," he said in a statement.
Wan Saiful, who said he had personally represented Perikatan Nasional (PN) in a series of meetings with Barisan Nasional (BN) during the campaign, congratulated BN on winning 18 state seats and PN on claiming seven.
"This victory forming a state government with a two-thirds majority is not a coincidence.
"It is clear evidence of the effectiveness of the strategic cooperation we have built together between BN and PN," he said.
He said the coordination between the two coalitions had been relentless, unifying their machinery to ensure candidates were introduced and well received by voters across every constituency.
Wan Saiful also issued a pointed message to DAP, wishing the party "good luck" in the upcoming Melaka election and saying the signal from voters in Johor and Negri Sembilan had been unmistakable.
"This blue unity wave will not stop and we are ready to face it again in Melaka," he said.

Title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja, team killed in Pakistan avalanche
Article:
SKARDU: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja and his nine climbing companions were all killed by an avalanche in Pakistan during an ascent of one of the world's highest mountains, his expedition company said on Saturday, as rescuers tackled treacherous conditions to recover their bodies.
The avalanche struck on Thursday, cutting off contact with the international expedition led by Purja, a 43-year-old British-Nepali climber, on Broad Peak in northern Pakistan.
"It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak," Purja's company Elite Expeditions said on social media.
"We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive," it said.
The remains recovered so far – flown by helicopter to hospital for formal identification – included an American woman, an Omani woman and a Nepali man, the regional government said in a statement released on Friday night.
Purja, who served with Britain's Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, broke multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide.
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah offered his condolences over the "tragic" deaths of Purja and the other climbers, which he said "has shocked us."
"The physical journey of all the deceased climbers... has been interrupted, but the history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring," Shah said in a statement on social media.
Police in the mountainous northern Gilgit-Baltistan region said in a statement that high-altitude porters and rescue teams were carrying out a second day of the operation on Saturday after the search was paused due to difficult weather conditions a day earlier.
Rescuers and military helicopters had been scouring the area and teams stayed at the base camp overnight, according to the regional government.
"The rescue operation is being conducted under extremely challenging terrain and high-altitude weather conditions by the Pakistani army in coordination with local high-altitude climbers and rescuers," it said.
The disaster prompted an outpouring of grief within Nepal and from the wider mountaineering community.
Italian great Reinhold Messner, who made the first solo ascent of Everest, paid tribute to Purja, saying his thoughts were with his friends and family.
"Nirmal chose his own path with courage and passion. What remains is not only the sorrow of his passing but the memory of a life truly lived," he said in a post on Instagram.
- POWERFUL AVALANCHE -
The avalanche struck while the mountaineers were attempting to summit Broad Peak (8,047 metres, or 26,400 feet) on Thursday at an altitude of around 6,600 metres, according to regional authorities.
The expedition comprised 10 people – including Purja, five Nepalis, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American and a climber from China.
The team was last in contact on Thursday morning, the official statement said, with reports emerging that evening of the powerful avalanche.
"Data from their tracking devices indicates that they were thrown hundreds of metres down the mountainside," Naila Kiani, from Pakistan's Alpine Club, told Le Monde newspaper.
Fida Ali, a climber in the area who worked closely with Purja since 2023, told AFP their focus for the climbing season was summiting Broad Peak but they had first tackled another mountain, G2, in harsh weather.
Ali also joined the expedition to Broad Peak in its initial stages but returned early to accompany a Russian climber who was feeling the effects of exhaustion – narrowly avoiding the fatal avalanche.
"I wanted to go with him (Purja) but couldn't and came back with her. I was part of the team but survived," he told AFP.
- SUPER PEAKS -
Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, said Purja's death was a "big loss."
"He showed Nepalis that climbing doesn't have to be just work, that you can climb for your own fun and passion," he told AFP.
Purja had written on X this week that he was close to becoming the first person to climb all 14 "super peaks" twice without oxygen.
"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down," he wrote.
He had climbed all 14 "eight-thousanders" (peaksabove 8,000 metres) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 – then a record.
Broad Peak is the world's 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range in northern Pakistan, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000-metre-plus ascents.
It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.--AFP

Title: Bersatu to explore coalition with moderate parties after Negri polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu said it will discuss forming a coalition with moderate and progressive parties to inject fresh energy into the country's democracy following its solo outing in the Negri Sembilan election.
In a statement, the party said the move would be pursued "for a brighter future".
"Bersatu will discuss the formation of a coalition of moderate and progressive parties to revitalise democracy in the country for a brighter future," it said.
The party also congratulated BN on securing a fresh mandate to form the Negri Sembilan government in the 16th state election and said it accepted the decision of voters who backed its candidates in the 24 seats it contested under its own logo.
"This is the first time Bersatu has contested an election using its own logo without depending on or riding on another party.
"The outcome requires Bersatu to take bold steps to strengthen internal discipline, work harder and pursue a reform agenda that delivers the best outcomes for the people," it said.
Bersatu also thanked its machinery for working tirelessly to support the party's candidates in a spirit of solidarity and loyalty.
The party said it would study the results in detail and conduct a post-mortem to identify strategic measures to strengthen its position going forward.
The statement, issued by Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, followed the Aug 1 Negri Sembilan
election
, in which Bersatu broke ranks with its PN partners to contest 24 seats independently after splitting from Pas earlier this year.
BN and PN, which reached an electoral
understanding
to avoid multi-cornered contests, unofficially secured 25 of the 36 seats contested.
Speaking after the results were announced, Azmin said the party would discuss forming a coalition with "moderate and progressive parties" and confirmed Bersatu would conduct a post-mortem on its election performance to identify strategic measures to strengthen its position.
His remarks came after months of speculation over Bersatu's standing within PN following Pas' decision in June to sever ties with the party and Bersatu's insistence, through Azmin, that it remained a
registered
political party with no reason to be dissolved despite calls for its members to return to Umno.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said BN and PN had
swept
every Malay-majority seat and also wrested two DAP strongholds, including Chennah, previously held by DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Caretaker MB Aminuddin loses Linggi by nearly 3,000 votes in Negri Sembilan polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Caretaker Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun suffered a crushing defeat in the Linggi state seat, losing to Barisan Nasional's Mohd Faizal Ramli by a majority of 2,976 votes.
Aminuddin, who is also state Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, fell heavily in a seat he had chosen to contest over his traditional Sikamat stronghold, where he had served as assemblyman for four consecutive terms.
BN's retention of Linggi formed part of a sweeping night for the coalition, which claimed 18 of the 36 seats in the Negri Sembilan state assembly, with BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) together surpassing the two-thirds majority threshold with 25 seats combined.

Title: Anwar congratulates BN on Negri win, pledges federal support
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Barisan Nasional (BN) on its victory in the Negri Sembilan election.
Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, pledged that the federal government would continue to support the new state government for the welfare and prosperity of the state and its people.
In a post on social media, Anwar also expressed his highest appreciation to all voters who had participated earnestly in the democratic process.
He also expressed his appreciation to the people of Negri Sembilan for placing their trust in PH and caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun over the past eight years.
"Throughout that period, Pakatan Harapan has left behind a legacy of excellent governance based on good administration, stability and development that has benefited the people.
"May this legacy continue to be strengthened for the progress of Negri Sembilan," he said.
BN and PN unofficially secured 25 of Negri Sembilan's 36 seats in the state election earlier today, with BN winning 18 seats and PN seven, surpassing the two-thirds majority needed to form the government.
PH's night was marked by the loss of two of its most prominent figures — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke, who lost the Chennah seat he had held for three consecutive terms, and Aminuddin himself, who fell in Linggi in a seat he had chosen over his traditional Sikamat stronghold.

Title: When a rumour sparked a rush for Europe
Article:
When Fatima Zahra heard the rumour of a rare border opening between Morocco and Spain, she joined thousands in rushing to attempt a perilous journey into the Ceuta enclave by land or sea.
AFP images showed people swimming around Ceuta's frontier fence and others clambering over barbed wire to reach European soil, as Moroccan riot police fired tear gas and water cannon at crowds after an apparent breakdown of border controls.
An AFP journalist on the scene witnessed the arrest of around 30 young people.
Ceuta, a Spanish territory of 18.5 square kilometres in north Africa, and the similar enclave Melilla, have Europe's only two land borders with its southern neighbouring continent.
Zahra was eventually turned away at the Moroccan border town of Fnideq, but Ceuta's regional president said some 60,000 people had successfully entered the tiny territory of just 80,000 residents.
"I was in Tangier, where I was working. I woke up in the morning and heard that Ceuta had opened," Zahra said.
"At that point, I told the people with me let's go there for work... let's try our luck, too," she added, saying she wanted to leave for Europe because she works "under appalling conditions".
The square near Fnideq from which many had set out the day before was a scene of ruin on Friday after the clashes, with more than a dozen cars burned out and rocks littering the ground as officers tried to push hopeful migrants back.
Ceuta's regional president said at least 34 people had lost their lives in the treacherous dash into the territory.
Footage of the border chaos has sparked a crisis for Spain's left-wing government.
Madrid has sent troops to boost security, while France announced tighter checks on its border with Spain, and Italy called for the country to be suspended from Europe's open-borders Schengen zone.
But for locals, the chance of a better life in Europe was worth the risk, even in the perilous currents of the Strait of Gibraltar.
Karim, another would-be migrant turned back, said news of some successful crossings emboldened many to make their own attempt.
"Suddenly, they heard that the borders were open and that some young people had crossed, so everyone ended up here," he said.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez visited the enclave on Friday after the largest inflow of people into the autonomous city since May 2021.
He said he would "characterise what happened... as an attack, a violation on Spain's territorial integrity".
The images of ebullient arrivals to Spain, a portion of them minors and some wearing only swimsuits and flip-flops, have spread far and wide, threatening a rupture in relations with Rabat.
While Spanish police in Ceuta appeared to do little to intervene, some jubilant migrants walked through its streets, calling out: "Bye bye Morocco, hello Spain."
Local Spanish television station El Faro broadcast footage showing young people, including a 14-year-old girl, making the "V" for victory sign after crossing into the European nation.
At dawn, the Moroccan police response became heavier as dozens of officers used water cannon and tear gas to push back those trying to leave Morocco, with some elderly women escorted from the scene of the clashes.
Members of the crowd responded by throwing stones and using slingshots, according to an AFP journalist.
Fires engulfed dozens of cars, including informal taxis in which some had arrived the previous day.
By the afternoon, the clashes had stopped and trucks were clearing away the burnt vehicles.
AFP footage showed dozens of young people turned back from Ceuta scattering into the countryside.
Some had made long journeys from cities as far away as Marrakesh and Kenitra after hearing of a chance to reach European soil.
Abdelhakim, also turned back from the Spanish territory, said he walked 14km "through the mountains" to reach the Morocco-Spain border, which he also believed was open.
"Once we got here, we were told to cross by sea. I found myself completely submerged and saw two men die right before my eyes," he said.
"That's when I backed away and remembered that I have two children of my own, and that I couldn't risk my life."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hadi says success in Negri will spark a 'bigger wave of change'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas president Datuk Seri Abdul Hadi Awang expressed his appreciation to voters in Negri Sembilan for placing their trust in Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the state election.
In a statement, he said the result was a clear signal that the people had accepted efforts towards unity among Muslims rooted in justice, welfare and harmony within a plural society.
"InsyaAllah, this success will spark a bigger wave of change in efforts to restore the country, while building a clean, caring and stable administration," he said.
"Pas is mindful of the great responsibility and trust placed upon it.
"The priority now is to fulfil this victory through a welfare-driven, upright and fair agenda for all," he said.
He also thanked the leadership of both PN and Barisan Nasional (BN), as well as candidates, workers and party machinery, for working as one to secure the coalitions' victory.
"May Allah SWT grant us guidance and strength to fulfil the people's mandate to the best of our ability," he said.
His statement follows today's state election, in which BN and PN unofficially secured
25 of the 36 seats contested,
surpassing the two-thirds majority needed to form the state government.
In the days leading up to polling day,
Hadi had directed Pas members
and supporters to vote for BN candidates in seats not contested by PN, describing it as part of the coalitions' strategy to avoid splitting votes.
He said the same approach had been used to deliver BN's landslide win in the Johor state election last month, with Pas acting as the "defensive line" while BN led the charge, and that if the cooperation succeeded in Negri Sembilan, the same model would continue to be strengthened going forward.

Title: NS polls: Loke, Aminuddin among biggest casualties as BN wins 18 seats
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BN swept to 18 seats in the 36-seat Negri Sembilan state assembly, delivering a crushing blow to PH as DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke and caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun were among its biggest casualties, while BN and PN combined to secure a two-thirds majority.
Based on unofficial results, BN won Chennah, Pertang, Sungai Lui, Palong, Jeram Padang, Lenggeng, Juasseh, Seri Menanti, Senaling, Pilah, Johol, Labu, Chembong, Rantau, Kota, Linggi, Gemencheh and Repah.
PN won seven seats — Klawang, Serting, Sikamat, Ampangan, Paroi, Bagan Pinang and Gemas — with the latter marking Parti Wawasan's first-ever state seat victory.
Together, BN and PN secured 25 of the 36 seats in the Negri Sembilan state assembly, surpassing the 24-seat threshold required for a two-thirds majority. PH won the remaining 11 seats, based on the unofficial count.
The result marks a dramatic turnaround from the 2023 state election, when BN won 14 seats and PN secured five. PH, which had governed Negri Sembilan since 2018, was reduced to 11 seats and lost control of the state government.
The night's biggest casualties were Loke and Aminuddin.
Loke, who had served as the Chennah assemblyman for three consecutive terms, lost to MCA's Siow Kong Choon.
According to Sin Chew Daily, Loke said he was considering stepping down as Negri Sembilan DAP chairman to take responsibility for the party's performance in today's election.
Aminuddin, popularly known as Tok Min, lost the Linggi seat — which he chose to contest instead of defending his traditional Sikamat stronghold, which he had held for four terms — to Mohd Faizal Ramli in a three-cornered contest.
The results also ended the tenure of four-term PH incumbent Veerapan Superamaniam, who is also a state executive councillor, after he lost the Repah seat.
Among BN's winners was Negri Sembilan Umno chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, who retained Pertang after defeating PH's Mohd Umry Abdul Khois and Bersatu's Mohd Faizal Fadli Mohd Idrus.
Jalaluddin previously represented Pertang from 2013 to 2018 before regaining the seat in the 2023 state election.
Meanwhile, Parti Wawasan's Ridzuan Ahmad delivered the party's first-ever state seat by winning Gemas, while PN's Danni Rais won Klawang.

Title: AI is rewriting Asia's air cargo story
Article:
The global race to build artificial intelligence is redrawing Asia's air cargo map, prompting airlines to redesign networks around growing semiconductor manufacturing hubs as cross-border ecommerce loses momentum.
Unlike the post-pandemic parcel boom, demand tied to AI infrastructure is underpinned by multi-year orders for advanced memory chips and processors and hundreds of billions of dollars of planned investment in data centres, airlines and logistics companies say.
At the same time, tighter lowvalue import rules in the United States and Europe are dampening the cross-border e-commerce trade that has driven much of the industry's recent growth.
"E-commerce was air freight's single biggest growth pillar, but that is no longer the case," Niall van de Wouw, chief airfreight officer at Xeneta, said when the freight analytics firm issued its mid-year outlook last month.
Korean Air offers one of the clearest examples of the transition. Cargo revenue surged 46 per cent in the second quarter to 1.54 trillion won (US$1.07 billion), driven by AI chips, server racks and data centre infrastructure that the airline said had replaced e-commerce shipments from China as its primary growth engine.
Advanced high-tech cargo "has rapidly expanded as a core growth driver", said Jaedong Eum, executive vice-president and head of Korean Air's cargo business.
Demand is unusually visible, he said, with orders for advanced high-bandwidth memory chips and processors already stretching two to three years into the future even as demand continues to exceed supply.
Global semiconductor sales more than doubled year-on-year in April, the strongest growth since records began in 1986, according to Xeneta.
By contrast, China's low-value and e-commerce exports fell seven per cent in May, marking a sixth consecutive monthly decline.
The US ended duty-free de minimis treatment for low-value imports from China last year, while the European Union this month abolished its own dutyfree threshold.
Japan's ANA Holdings said in a statement that the EU move was a downside risk for the broader cargo market even as semiconductor-related shipments remained strong.
Japan exports semiconductor manufacturing equipment, South Korea produces advanced memory chips and Taiwan is the centre of leading-edge chip production.
Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand and Singapore are emerging as increasingly important manufacturing and assembly hubs for AI servers destined for North America and Europe.
Freight throughput at Singapore's Changi Airport grew 8.7 per cent year-on-year in the first half driven by strong global semiconductor demand, said Lim Ching Kiat, the airport group's executive vice-president for air hub and cargo development.
Airlines are reorganising around those flows.
Japan Airlines said technology products accounted for about 80 per cent of the increase in air exports from Asia excluding China over the past year, underscoring how semiconductor and AI-related hardware is reshaping regional cargo flows. It has expanded freighter services linking semiconductor hubs such as Taipei, Bangkok and Hanoi with Tokyo's Narita airport.
In Taiwan, China Airlines has added Southeast Asia freighter flights as manufacturers diversify production and said AI-related demand helped lift cargo volumes 8.1 per cent in the first half of the year.
EVA Airways said AI-related shipments now account for up to half of its cargo revenue.
Airlines say AI hardware requires different handling from traditional air freight because shipments often include delicate, high-value semiconductor manufacturing equipment, graphics processors and complete server racks.
Airline group IATA estimates AI-related goods accounted for 53.5 per cent of the value of goods carried by air last year while making up just seven per cent of cargo volume.
To adapt to the changing market, Cathay Pacific Airways said it had introduced software that automatically determines how sensitive semiconductor equipment and AI hardware should be loaded and secured inside aircraft.
The surge is also stretching cargo infrastructure.
Dimerco Express Group said AI and semiconductor shipments had filled Taiwan's Taipei air cargo hub to capacity last month, keeping freight space tight on routes to the US and within Asia.
"As major tech companies introduce next-generation AI processors and continue their longterm infrastructure commitments, we anticipate strong cargo demand to persist through the second half of 2026," Korean Air's Eum said.
The writers are from Reuters

Title: NST Leader: Tabung Haji and the price of greed
Article:
When greed, poor governance and financial mismanagement come together, they can bring down mighty institutions.
They almost did it to Tabung Haji, which manages billions of ringgit in Muslim depositors' funds.
The mighty 63-year-old institution, burdened by RM12.6 billion in investment losses, was on the verge of collapse, we are being told.
It had all the scars of huge losses and failed business ventures, compelling the government to come to its aid.
We are not surprised. Greed, poor governance and financial mismanagement are Malaysian diseases of old. Add to these another maiming Malaysian malady — political interference — then you get a serial institution-killer.
Calls to end political appointments in government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies are already getting louder with the Centre to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4) saying that the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji has laid bare the consequences of political interference in such entities.
To C4, such appointments carried inherent corruption risks by entrenching crony networks, where political considerations often took precedence over sound financial management.
This leads us to an overwhelming question: ancient as these ailments are, why haven't we put an end to them? The question has long ago answered itself: there is a lack of accountability.
Transparency International Malaysia in its analysis of the Auditor-General's Report 2/2025 highlighting irregularities amounting to RM48.87 billion concluded thus: Malaysia's public sector suffers from systemic governance failures and a culture of impunity rather than isolated incidents of mismanagement.
Little wonder, despite audit report after audit report highlighting leakages and wastage of taxpayers' money we seldom hear of anyone being held accountable.
Accountability doesn't just mean making errant officers answerable but also holding their leadership responsible.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) eight-member special task force, we learn, began scrutinising Tabung Haji records related to the RCI findings on Friday.
But couldn't the MACC have stepped in earlier? Previously, the MACC had said that it can only investigate if it had reason to suspect offences under the MACC Act.
But Tabung Haji's debacle has been made public by the media for several years now. Wasn't this enough to launch an investigation?
Be that as it may, we are glad that the MACC has stepped in as soon as the RCI report was made public.
We applaud the MACC for casting the net wider to probe bigger issues not covered by the RCI report such as whether there were elements of corruption, abuse of power or misappropriation.
The MACC has also made known that its investigation would not be confined to any specific period of Tabung Haji's leadership.
Let this be the beginning of the accountability journey for those who manage public funds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri victory strengthens case for BN-PN cooperation in Melaka, say analysts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BN and PN should maintain their electoral cooperation in Melaka following their sweep in the Negri Sembilan election, but should avoid formalising the arrangement, political analysts said.
Universiti Sains Malaysia political analyst Professor Datuk Dr Sivamurugan Pandian said the cooperation made clear strategic sense but cautioned against rushing into a formal alliance.
"It is strategically wise for BN and PN to continue cooperating in Melaka, especially to avoid splitting the Malay vote and consolidate their position. However, they should maintain electoral cooperation rather than rush into a formal alliance," he told the New Straits Times.
He said Melaka would serve as the next test of whether the BN-PN formula used in Johor and the Negri Sembilan election could become a broader political trend.
He added that both coalitions should coordinate seat allocations while retaining their separate identities to preserve their tactical understanding.
Earlier today, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the understanding between the two coalitions would continue in Melaka, adding that the Negri Sembilan result would strengthen the
momentum
of what he described as the "blue" and "dark blue" political wave that began in Johor.
International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri agreed that continued cooperation was the most sensible path forward.
"I think this is the best option going forward for BN and PN to avoid splitting the Malay vote.
"Negri Sembilan was a testing ground and the strategy has proven successful, so why not continue it in Melaka?" she said.
Syaza said the two coalitions would likely continue describing the arrangement as an electoral pact rather than declare a formal alliance, but warned that the formula could face challenges in the northern states.
"I think they might start to face trouble the further north they go," she said.
Universiti Utara Malaysia political analyst Dr Kamarul Zaman Yusoff said the BN-PN momentum was likely to carry into Melaka despite differences in the state's political landscape.
He said the same overarching theme of Malay-Muslim political dominance had been consistently employed across the Johor, Negri Sembilan and prospective Melaka elections.
"BN has been gaining momentum since Johor, followed by its stronger performance in the Negri Sembilan election. Of course, that momentum will be carried into Melaka, even though the situation there is somewhat different," he said.
Kamarul attributed PH's defeat in the Negri Sembilan election primarily to the strong consolidation of Malay votes behind BN and PN.
"There is very strong consolidation of Malay votes. Although the transferability of votes between BN and PN has yet to be fully achieved, the rate is very encouraging," he said.
He added that PH's voter base had remained largely intact, but the consolidation on the opposing side was enough to overcome it.
BN and PN unofficially secured 25 of the 36 seats in the Negri Sembilan election on Aug 1, with BN
winning
18 seats and PN seven, surpassing the two-thirds majority required to form the state government.
Zahid said the result would strengthen the "blue wave" that began in Johor, adding that both coalitions would hold further talks on forming a stable state government, subject to the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan and the state's four Undang.
Before the Negri Sembilan election, Zahid had said the same BN-PN understanding would
extend
to Melaka, where the Legislative Assembly's term expires by late December.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had earlier said Melaka could go to the polls by September, following the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police hunt motorcyclist after roadside brawl at Port Klang junction goes viral
Article:
SHAH ALAM: South Klang police are hunting an unidentified motorcyclist following a roadside brawl at the junction of Jalan Kastam that was captured on video and has since gone viral on social media.
The incident took place at around 3.30pm on July 29, when a 30-year-old local male car driver came to blows with the motorcyclist at the junction, district police chief Assistant Commissioner Lim Jit Huey said in a statement today.
He said the cause of the altercation was still under investigation and that police were actively tracking down the motorcyclist involved.
A case paper has been opened under Section 160 of the Penal Code for affray, which carries a maximum prison sentence of six months, a fine of up to RM1,000, or both.
The case is also being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for improper use of network services, which carries a maximum prison sentence of one year or a fine.
Police urged members of the public with any information related to the case to come forward and assist with investigations by contacting investigating officer Inspector Mohd Shauqhi Abdul Shukor at 011-51691730, the South Klang police operations room at 03-33762222, or the nearest police station.
